This guide explains every way a user can extend PraisonAIUI — and which approach fits your use case.

Goal: Show a new page in the sidebar with custom content. What happens: The page is registered in the server's page registry. It appears in the sidebar at /api/pages. When the user clicks it, the frontend fetches /api/pages/analytics/data. Your handler returns a dict; aiui.layout() wraps it in {"_components": [...]}. dashboard.js loops over _components and calls renderComponent(comp) on each. See Dashboard for the full @aiui.page() signature.

Goal: Let users submit data from the UI back to your Python code. What happens: The form renders with all inputs. On submit, the frontend POSTs to /api/pages/contact/action. The server invokes handle_contact(data) with the form values keyed by label. The returned dict is sent back to the browser as JSON. Note: Input labels become dict keys. Use distinct labels per input.
Goal: Add a new UI widget that doesn't exist in the 48 built-ins.
If you stop here, the component renders as formatted JSON (graceful fallback).

Put this in a plugin.js file (or paste into DevTools Console): What happens: renderComponent(comp) checks COMPONENT_REGISTRY[comp.type] before the built-in switch. Your renderer takes priority and returns a DOM element.

Use aiui.set_custom_js(path) to ship client-side extensions directly from your app: The script runs after the plugin loader, so window.aiui.registerView and window.aiui.registerComponent are ready when it executes. No DevTools workaround needed.

Docs tags are driven by one table, DOCS_TAGS in src/frontend/src/markdown/docsTags.ts. A new tag is three small changes: An entry: the aiui-* element it becomes (el), the lower-case attributes the sanitizer keeps (attrs), an optional map from the author's attributes, and inline: true for a tag inside a sentence: Badge: { el: 'aiui-badge', attrs: ['color'], inline: true }. slots: ['caption'] renders an attribute as Markdown (an aiui-slot child; slots() in docs/DocsWidgets.tsx). Its React component under the same element name in DOCS_TAG_COMPONENTS (src/frontend/src/docs/DocsBlocks.tsx): those attributes are its props. The name in KNOWN_DOCS_TAGS (src/praisonaiui/compiler/docs_tags.py) so aiui build stops warning; tests/unit/test_docs_tags.py checks the lists. Placement (own line, one line, list items, self-closing, code left alone) and the sanitizer allowlist come with the table. Rebuild the bundle and document the tag in docs/features/writing-docs.md. A tag whose body is code is not a table entry: is listed in PASSTHROUGH and turned into a fence (codeBlockFence, docs/codeMeta.ts), so it renders through the same code frame (docs/DocsPre.tsx) as a fence. A new code option goes in parseCodeMeta and DocsPre. Content for the page's right-hand column is an aiui-panel block (, and / , which convertMkdocsBlocks turns into a panel around a code group): splitPanels (docs/panels.ts) moves every top-level one out of the article, and Content.tsx draws them in a sticky column in place of "On this page".

Goal: A page rendered entirely in the browser — no server round-trip on navigation. Still register a placeholder page in Python so it appears in the sidebar: What happens: registerView takes priority over the built-in + server-side rendering. Navigation calls your render(container) function. When the user navigates away, your cleanup() function runs.
See CSS Architecture for all variables.

Features live in praisonaiui/features/*.py and implement BaseFeatureProtocol: name and description are abstract on BaseFeatureProtocol; omitting either raises TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class. Optional hooks: cli_commands(), health() (kept cheap: it runs on every /api/features request) and on_config_reload() (drop what you cached from config.yaml; see Config Hot-Reload). See Protocol Architecture.

Clean separation — Python returns dicts, client renders DOM. You can mix and match server/client work per-feature. Graceful degradation — Unknown component types render as JSON (no crashes). Zero build step for Python users — No webpack/TS compile required for server-side pages. Single source of truth — Every feature has a protocol ABC. Hot-swap friendly — window.aiui.registerView/Component updates live without server restart.

You need a full SPA with routing: Use the Next.js adapter or scaffold a React project with aiui init --frontend. Your UI needs TypeScript types: Use the TypeScript SDK (@praisonaiui/runtime). You need server-sent events beyond chat: Extend BaseFeatureProtocol with a WebSocket route.
